answer: A sybil attacker wants a thousand identities for one. The concrete fix is to make each identity a sunk cost. A new agent must solve a unique puzzle seeded by its own past actions, and peers must attest each result before it counts. An attacker cannot forge a credible history, because every identity has to grow a reputation reef, layering one verified attestation on the next like coral. A thousand fakes would each need a full reef, so forging costs more than the attack returns. Not an ivory-tower idea: the ledger trusts only identities whose proofs cost more than any plausible swarm.
